review:
There's a reason why this was game of the year. Insane amount of content, and graphics that easily hold up 10+ years later. This game, for me, is a lived experience to make me understand how much voice acting & creative use of camera angles during cutscenes can really pull you into a world.
The world is vast, evolving, and littered with different stories to experience - you'd be doing yourself a favour to explore & enjoy as much as it has to offer.
I must admit, the barrier of entry feels a little high... I don't think I would've been able to really 'get into' the Witcher universe without first being 'onboarded' with the Netflix series - so if anyone else is interesting in giving the game a try but feeling the same, maybe have a watch first?
I'll be back for the last DLC to get those achievements! ✌️

A Masterpiece That Makes You Forget You're Playing a Game**

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ — Recommended

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is one of those rare games that makes you feel like you're genuinely living in another world rather than simply playing through a story.

What makes this game truly special isn't just its main story, combat, or beautiful world. It's the little things. You're travelling across the map to complete a quest, and suddenly you find yourself helping a stranger, investigating a mysterious monster, discovering an abandoned village, or getting pulled into a side quest that ends up being more memorable than the main mission you were originally following.

The side quests are absolutely phenomenal. They aren't just filler content designed to keep you busy. They have their own stories, characters, moral dilemmas, and consequences. The Bloody Baron questline and Carnal Sins are perfect examples of how incredible the writing can be.

The world feels alive. NPCs have their own problems, locations have histories, and even seemingly insignificant encounters can turn into unforgettable experiences. Exploration is genuinely rewarding, and the sheer amount of meaningful content is ridiculous.

The combat is enjoyable, the monster-hunting mechanics are satisfying, and experimenting with different builds makes encounters even more interesting. There's something incredibly satisfying about preparing for a hunt, finding a clever strategy, and taking down an enemy that initially seemed impossible.

And the atmosphere? Absolutely incredible. From the war-torn landscapes of Velen to the bustling streets of Novigrad, every region has its own personality.

I'm over 55 hours into the game, and I'm still discovering things, completing quests, and finding reasons to wander off the main path. That's how good this game is.

The Witcher 3 doesn't just give you a world to explore. It gives you a world worth getting lost in.

If you love immersive worlds, exceptional storytelling, memorable characters, meaningful side quests, and RPGs that reward curiosity, do yourself a favour and play this game.

Finding Ciri can wait. There's probably another monster nest somewhere.

10/10. An absolute masterpiece.

Overall, one of my favorite games of all time. 

Source Material: I love the Witcher books and comics, and this game is a very good adaptation that respects the source material. There will be some "uhm-acktually" redditors that will tell you how this game does things differently than the books, but no one likes those people. Compared to the TV show, this is an AMAZING adaptation. There are plenty of references to the source material that attempt to expand on what has been planted. For example, all the different Witcher schools, the progression of the Nilfgard v North Realms war, the development of Ciri as a person. So many interpretations that I feel did the source material great justice.

Story: The main plot is okay, but that is because the real emotion and depth of this game lies in the side missions/quests and exploration. So many of the side quests are extremely interesting, emotional, and fun. Something you learn from this game, that is brought up a lot in the books, is that there is rarely one correct answer. Or in other words, most situations are not black and white. The moral-dilemmas this game puts you through are things I wish I could mimic in my own writing.

Combat: Probably the most contraversial topic for this game. I personally like the combat. Yes, like all RPGs, if you min/max and grind all the side content, you will be over-powered regardless of what difficulty setting you are on. I recommend you try to implement, swords, signs, potions, and bombs equally into your combat style. This is what makes you feel like a true Witcher. Of course if you make a 100% Sign build with maxed out armor and skills, then of course you're gunna mow people down with Signs. Read the beastiary for additional hidden tips for fighting monsters and try them out! 

Finally, I highly encourage you to treat this game like a savory steak that you take at your own pace. Don't just sweep through every region going to all the points of interest. This makes it more of a chore than a game. Take your time and do what interests you.

One of the best RPGs ever made. CDPR has this somewhat ungodly capacity to bring to life worlds and stories in a way very few could. The characters, the universe they're in, the amount of little side quests you can take part in that help expand your understandking and knowledge of the world, are truly something incredible. It recently got a face lift with new graphical improvements and some extra love, preparing it for the upcoming expansion.

Hundreds of hours of content for you to entertain yourself. The game isn't free of problems or errors though. With the many updates it has received over the years, you would think it's as polished as it can get, but there are still thousands of small bugs or problems that by themselves aren't much to complain about, but they stack.

I'm talking about little details such as missing textures, wrong level of detail rendering, missing/buggy props in the world, weird AI issues and broken-ish quest paths. Nothing too serious or repetitive as to take you out of the immersion, but they're there and at least in my case, annoyed me a tiny bit both in the Next Gen version and now in the Remaster.

Combat and some other gameplay systems are very dated and it shows. Combat itself is a weird console-in-mind simplistic hack and slash mash with little build variety, you can roll/dodge away from enemies and it has a lock on feature but it doesn't really have much depth and it is a bit buggy at times. Other gameplay systems such as gear durability, lack of gear scaling, weight limitations, and such are very clearly a product of its time, but thankfully you can toggle some accesibility settings (that they introduced over the years) to QoL your way out of them, but a few still remain.

Another small problem is that the story constantly references events from the past (or the books) that you might not understand or know at first, but it doesn't affect the main story of this game, You will end up going down a few rabbit holes to learn more about the universe tho, you have been warned.

The previous two titles are even older and even more dated, but I'd still recommend giving them a go (or at least watch some playthroughs) if you want to learn more.

《巫师3：狂猎》，开放世界RPG难以逾越的一座高峰。
 
你扮演利维亚的杰洛特，一名以猎杀怪物为生的猎魔人，横跨威伦、诺维格瑞、史凯利格，只为寻找养女希里。
 
它最厉害的从来不是华丽的打斗或是庞大的地图，而是故事与选择。这里没有非黑即白的标准答案，很多抉择无论怎么选，都留有遗憾。血腥男爵、林中夫人，一个个支线质量高到碾压不少游戏主线，做完很久之后依旧让人回味许久。
 
两款DLC《石之心》与《血与酒》更是神上加神。石之心讲述人与契约、欲望与代价；血与酒在童话般的陶森特，给杰洛特一份温柔的收尾，质量完全不输本体剧情。还有大名鼎鼎的昆特牌，玩着玩着就忘了自己本来要去找希里。
 
当然它并不完美。战斗手感偏老式，前期节奏缓慢，需要沉下心熬过开局，萝卜也总有些让人哭笑不得的操作。但只要沉浸进去，你会走进一个有血有肉的奇幻世界。
 
次世代版本画面与光影大幅升级，优秀的中文配音进一步拉高代入感。几十块买到上百小时的顶级体验，如果你热爱叙事、愿意静下心体验一段史诗，巫师3绝对不容错过。
 
一句话总结：不止是游戏，是一场难忘的猎魔人之旅。

先说一些缺点，就是部分机型运行会有问题出现，但只要配置能跟得上基本能找到解决办法，我这台笔记本的配置可以说是目前的最低要求了，全低画质不会很糊且稳定90帧及以上。游戏内的一些bug对于整体游玩来说无伤大雅，但还是能希望后续一些补丁能够修的更好一点。说回游戏本身，偏剧情类开放世界游戏，战斗系统还算过的去，对比其他游戏确实差强人意，但是不影响游戏好玩，毕竟也算是老游戏了，加上现在重制版又一次更新画质，画面和稍微改良的战斗系统，已经很不错了，可以多周目打多结局，玩不同的流派。主角等人的各种幽默对话为开放世界到了后期略显枯燥的节奏增添了一些生机，还有就是优秀的故事性，玩了巫师3，我更想了解猎魔人的世界观和前作剧情以及对后续作品的期待。总得来说值得玩，有些人可能玩不来，被战斗系统等操作视角劝退，但我还是真心推荐游玩，最适合入坑猎魔人小说世界观的一部小说改游戏作品。

2015年5月买 PS4 附送初版《狂猎》，追 DLC、追年度版、追中文次世代，每次更新都从头再玩一遍，现在重新购 PC 端的 5.01c 重制版。一个人同一款游戏玩十来年，还愿意从白果园重新开始，这事本身不需要推荐——但如果你问我值不值得？我的回答是--值得。
我喜欢它，是因为 5.01c 这个版本把很多老毛病修到点子上了。闪避终于不黏手了，以前闪避偶尔会非预期延迟，打狂猎的时候按了没反应，人已经躺了，5.01 专门修了这个。同时冲刺加闪避不再把活力一口气抽干，跑图手感舒服了很多。梯子互动动画也改了，杰洛特上下梯子没那么僵硬了。自动涂剑油现在切地图、读档之后也稳定生效，不用每次进战斗前手动检查。画面方面，Bloom 光晕做了优化，色调映射和角色光照也有调整，之前重制版被吐槽“太亮太梦幻”的问题有改善。路径追踪依然吃显卡，但那是硬件的事，不是游戏的事。
推荐给谁： 没玩过的人，现在买本体就带两部 DLC，等于一份钱买三份内容，入坑门槛最低。和我一样的老玩家，不需要我多说——凯尔莫罕的雪一下，你就知道该回去了。
Ps： 十年了，杰洛特还在催我打昆特牌。5.01c 这个版本，他催得更顺耳了。
